Other Upstream Issues, Checked Against Current Code

Source: vignettes/articles/other-upstream-issues.Rmd
other-upstream-issues.Rmd

Why this exists

Beyond the three issues covered in the code fixes article, ices-tools-prod/icesDatras has a number of other issues, most closed, some open, going back years. This checks a representative set of them directly, against a clean copy of current master – not the fork, not assumptions – to see which still apply and which have already been resolved some other way over time.

Most of what follows is good news: issues that are old don’t necessarily mean issues that are still broken.

Draft follow-up comments for the three issues most directly resolved by this fork’s own work are collected at the end, ready to copy into the actual GitHub issues when it’s time to post them – nothing here has been sent anywhere yet.

Already resolved – confirmed, not assumed

Six issues checked this way no longer reproduce at all on current master:

  • “set variable type” (#45) – reported bind_rows() failing across two calls because GearEx came back character in one and integer in the other. Re-running the exact reproduction from the issue: both calls now return GearEx as character, and both rbind() and bind_rows() succeed.
  • “getCatchWgt error” (#37) and “getcatchWgt not working” (#36) – both reported a “duplicate ‘row.names’ are not allowed” crash for specific survey/year/quarter/species combinations. Both exact reproductions now run cleanly.
  • “Wrongly identifying statsquare (StatRec) as integer” (#10) and “AreaCode format issue” (#30) – both about numeric-looking area codes (e.g. 44E3) losing their letter component when coerced to numeric. StatRec now comes back character as expected; simplify() already excludes both StatRec and AreaCode from its numeric-conversion pass.
  • “White spaces in character strings” (#2) – reported trailing whitespace on character fields ("GOV " instead of "GOV"). parseDatras() already trims whitespace on every field; no trailing spaces found on a live check.

None of these need anything from this fork – they were already fixed, just without an explanation of what changed attached to the closed issue.

Related to an issue, but not quite the same bug

Two issues don’t reproduce as originally reported, but each points at a real, still-open gap nearby that this fork hasn’t resolved either.

“get_datras_unaggregated_data("CA", …) issue” (#50)

The original report showed the first row of a getDatrasUnaggregated("CA", ...) call coming back as empty strings/NA across every column, with a stray byte-order-mark character contaminating the second row’s RecordHeader. Re-running the exact reproduction: neither symptom appears – the first rows are clean.

But the same call still throws three warnings unrelated to that original report:

getDatrasUnaggregated("CA", "NS-IBTS", "2025", "1")
#> Warning: Column name 'ScientificName_WoRMS' (colClasses[[1]][26]) not found
#> Warning: Column name 'NumberAtLength' (colClasses[[2]][6]) not found
#> Warning: Column name 'ValidAphiaID' (colClasses[[2]][7]) not found

This function has its own, separate, hand-maintained column-type list (.datras_column_classes()) that doesn’t go through getDatrasFieldList() at all – and that list currently declares three columns that don’t exist in the real downloaded data (under those exact names, at least). Harmless as a warning, but it confirms this list is out of sync with the actual current download-API schema. Not something this fork’s field-list work touches – that work is all on the SOAP-endpoint side, and this is a wholly separate code path.

“a webservice bug to be fixed in icesDatras” (#28)

The original report: a self-closing tag with no space before the slash, <Valid_Aphia/>, wasn’t recognised as a null field and became a malformed column. Re-running the exact historical query (NS-IBTS 1997 Q4) that the report used: Valid_Aphia now comes back as a perfectly clean column, last in the list – most likely because the underlying server response itself no longer emits that exact malformed tag for this query, not because any client-side code changed.

The underlying gap in the code is still there, confirmed directly:

gsub("^ *<(.*?) />$", "<\\1> NA </\\1>", "<Valid_Aphia/>")
#> [1] "<Valid_Aphia/>"     # unchanged -- the regex requires a space before "/>"
                            # and didn't match

This is a different regex from the one this fork’s own fixes touch (those fix name-extraction when a tag does have attributes and a space; this is the separate self-closing-tag-detection step, which still only matches <Tag />, not <Tag/>). Currently latent rather than active – nothing reproduces it live today – but the code itself was never made robust to the no-space form, so it’s one edge case away from resurfacing if a future response ever emits it again.

An open feature request, independently corroborated

“getSubmissionStatus_FishTrawlData” (#54) and its sibling “getSubmissionStatus_LitterData” (#55) ask for wrapper functions around two DATRAS webservice operations this package doesn’t currently expose at all. Confirmed directly: neither operation has any corresponding R function in this package, on either the fork or upstream – these are genuine, still-open gaps, not yet addressed anywhere.

Draft follow-up comments, ready to post

The three issues below are the ones this fork’s own work most directly resolves. Each draft is informative only – sharing findings and evidence, not requesting anything or announcing a pull request – and every code example has been checked against the current upstream master specifically, not the fork.

#48 – “getCPUELength - variable name returned”

I’ve been digging into this one, both the column-name issue in the original report and the Age_6-Age_15 “NA”-string companion issue from my earlier comment on this thread. Concrete repro against current master:

d <- getIndices(survey = "NS-IBTS", year = 1965, quarter = 1, species = 126417,
                fix_types = TRUE, new_names = TRUE)
grep("^Age", names(d), value = TRUE)
#>  [1] "AgePlusGroup"            "Age_0"                   "Age_1"
#>  [4] "Age_2"                   "Age_3"                   "Age_4"
#>  [7] "Age_5"                   "Age_6 xsi:nil=\"true\""  "Age_7 xsi:nil=\"true\""
#> [10] "Age_8 xsi:nil=\"true\""  "Age_9 xsi:nil=\"true\""  "Age_10 xsi:nil=\"true\""
#> [13] "Age_11 xsi:nil=\"true\"" "Age_12 xsi:nil=\"true\"" "Age_13 xsi:nil=\"true\""
#> [16] "Age_14 xsi:nil=\"true\"" "Age_15 xsi:nil=\"true\""

sapply(d[grep("xsi:nil", names(d))], class)
# every one of these comes back "character", holding the literal text "NA" --
# not a true NA

Root causes, for anyone else hitting this:

  1. Column name leak: parseDatras()’s name-extraction regex relies on a lazy quantifier ((.*?)) that isn’t reliably supported across regex engines. When DATRAS returns a self-closing null field like <Age_6 xsi:nil="true" />, the regex captures the whole tag content as the column name instead of just Age_6.
  2. The value-level companion bug, one level deeper: the same self-closing tag handling turns the field into the literal text "NA", not a true NA. -9 and "" are separately normalized to NA two lines later, but "NA" isn’t, and is.na("NA") is FALSE – so simplify()’s numeric-conversion guard gets fooled and leaves the whole column character.

I’ve got fixes for both working in my own fork for now – not filing a PR yet, still want to shake a few things out – but didn’t want this to sit without an update given it’s been a while. Happy to open one when it’s ready.

#46 – “on getCatchWgt”

Sharing something I found while looking into this more closely, might help pin down the actual scope of the question. Checked whether DataType == "C" hauls still need a HaulDuration/60-style conversion before use, comparing median catch-per-minute-towed by DataType (all species pooled, current master):

# NS-IBTS 2020 Q1
#        C         P         R
# 142129.22  91843.43  66711.43     <- C median ~2.1x the R median

# NS-IBTS 2024 Q1
#        C        P        R
# 128805.0 156413.4 133315.4        <- C and R medians ~1:1

So there’s a real, measurable gap in 2020 that’s gone by 2024. That lines up with the package’s own startup disclaimer (“known issues with the way CatCatchWgt has been reported until 2023”), so this looks like a real but time-bounded reporting-era issue on the data side, not something getCatchWgt() itself needs to compensate for going forward. Happy to share the full comparison script if useful.

#47 – “on getFlexFile”

Noting something related while looking at a few of these functions together – getCPUELength() and getCPUEAge() have the same gap described here, a bit worse. Checked against current master:

"StNo" %in% names(getFlexFile("NS-IBTS", 2022, 1, new_names = FALSE))
#> [1] FALSE
"Country" %in% names(getFlexFile("NS-IBTS", 2022, 1, new_names = FALSE))
#> [1] TRUE

"StNo" %in% names(getCPUELength("NS-IBTS", 2022, 1, new_names = FALSE))
#> [1] FALSE
"Country" %in% names(getCPUELength("NS-IBTS", 2022, 1, new_names = FALSE))
#> [1] FALSE     # getFlexFile at least keeps Country -- these two don't

Same result for getCPUEAge(). Might be worth folding into the same discussion rather than a separate report – looks like the same underlying cause: these “derived product” endpoints don’t carry the full haul-identifying columns HH/HL do.
